# The Bet · FinWise

> Module 1 · Ignite a PLG Motion. The growth hypothesis and where you're betting, plus the growth-loop visualization.

## Growth hypothesis

FinWise's biggest growth problem is FinWise's biggest growth problem is weak progression from trial to sustained paid use., because Only 128 of 6,424 trial starts appear as paid conversions, while the scenario reports just 40% one-year paid retention. I suspect users are not reaching enough useful, repeatable value; the root cause is not established by the table..

_Working notes: I think FinWise's biggest growth problem is weak progression from trials to sustained paid use. My hunch is that trial users do not reach enough practical, repeatable value early enough to justify paying and staying. Evidence: I think this because:
1. Only 2% of trial starters become paying customers.
2. Only 40% of paid customers remain after one year; 60% churn.
3. Most marketing spending goes to paid acquisition, but adding more acquisition spending no longer drives meaningful growth.
These observations support prioritizing the experience after acquisition. They do not prove that onboarding or collaboration is the root cause. Against the data: The specific data point that supports my view is that 6,424 trial starts produced just 128 paid conversions, or 1.99%, with the monthly ratio staying near 2%. This supports focusing on progression from trial to paid use. It does not confirm my proposed explanation about early value or collaboration; that remains a hypothesis to test._

_____

## The bet

The highest-leverage experiment I would run first is an optional invite-an-accountant-or-teammate step in trial onboarding, measured through week-1 activation before claiming downstream payment or retention gains.

**Not doing:** I am not increasing paid acquisition spending or prioritizing broad content and referral campaigns first, because focusing there would pull effort from learning whether existing trial accounts can reach useful shared value and convert.

_____

## Growth loop

**Loop type:** Collaboration, I would experiment with a collaboration loop because a small-business owner and a relevant accountant or teammate may reach useful financial outcomes together. If shared value creates repeat use, some collaborators may also bring another business into FinWise, connecting activation and engagement to distribution.
